title: God recalls telling Israel to listen and walk in His ways
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: 7:22 is the contrast half of the same recollection: sacrifice was not the command, hearing was. Cf. 1 Sam 15:22, Hos 6:6.

title: Jerusalem is told to cut off her hair and raise a lament
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Prophetic summons to mourn the rejected generation, like the recorded calls at 6:26, 9:17 and 22:10.

title: Israel is told to say false gods will perish from the earth
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Scripted answer to idolaters ('This is what you will say to them'); distinct from records 10:1–2 and 10:5.

title: Acknowledge that a person cannot direct his own steps
speaker: Jeremiah (in prayer)
note: Declarative maxim opening a prayer (10:23–25); only 10:23 teaches. Drop if sayings addressed to God are excluded.

title: Jeremiah is told to speak the covenant words to Judah
speaker: the Lord
note: 11:3 continues the charge ('you will say to them') with the curse on whoever will not hear; bridges records 11:2 and 11:4.

title: Jeremiah is told to deliver the saying of the filled wineskins
speaker: the Lord
note: Scripted saying and reply ('you will say to this people… then you will say'), like the recorded reply at 23:33.

title: Jeremiah is given the answer: to death, sword, famine and captivity
speaker: the Lord
note: Scripted reply to 'Where shall we go out?' Alternatively extend ot-jeremiah-v15-1 (15:1, 'Send this people away').

title: God calls Jeremiah to return and renews his commission as His mouth
speaker: the Lord
note: 15:19 (context verse) holds the directive: return, bring out the honored from the unworthy, do not turn to them; echoes 1:18.

title: Jeremiah is told how to answer when asked why disaster comes
speaker: the Lord
note: Scripted reply: their fathers abandoned God and did not keep His law, and this generation did worse.

title: God tells Jeremiah to smash the jar before the men with him
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The sign-act itself; 19:1 (get the jar) and 19:11 (Study Context, its meaning) are recorded, the smashing is not.

title: Do not build your house by injustice or withhold workers’ wages
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Ethical woe like Hab 2:6–12 (AUD-39-2-6); 22:15–16 ties judging the poor’s case to knowing God; echoes Lev 19:13 (C0607).

title: God orders Jeconiah recorded as an outcast with no heir enthroned
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Decree on Jeconiah’s line ('Record this man as an outcast'); compare the recorded naming order for Pharaoh Neco (26:17).

title: Egypt’s routed troops urge one another to flee home
speaker: Egypt’s soldiers (quoted in the oracle)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Quoted mutual exhortation inside the Egypt oracle; the catalogue records similar ones at 6:4–5 and 28:9–10.

title: The oracle calls for Babylon’s storehouses to be opened and destroyed
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 27:27 continues the same summons: 'Dry up all her fruits, and let them go down to slaughter.'

title: A prayer acknowledges the Lord’s declaration against Babylon
speaker: Jeremiah, relaying the Lord’s word
note: 28:61 opens Jeremiah’s charge ('When you arrive in Babylon… read all these words, and say'); consider retitling as the charge to Seraiah.

title: Jeremiah tells Seraiah to sink the scroll in the Euphrates
speaker: Jeremiah, relaying the Lord’s word
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The sign-act itself (bind a stone to the scroll, throw it in); record 28:64 holds only the interpreting words.

title: Attackers are told to set young warriors over Edom
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Brief war summons ('Appoint the young men over her') in the Edom oracle; the parallel line at 27:44 is first-person, not imperative.

title: Moab’s shattering is to be announced in Zogora
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 'Announce it in Zogora': a summons like recorded 27:2 (announce Babylon’s capture) and 31:17–19.

title: Moab’s neighbors are called to mourn the breaking of its power
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 31:20 continues the same summons: 'Wail and cry out; announce at Arnon that Moab perished.'

title: The cup pictures nations falling under the sword of judgment
speaker: the Lord
note: 32:28 continues the instruction: if they refuse the cup, say 'You will certainly drink.'

title: Testing claims to speak for God
speaker: Jeremiah, applying the Lord’s test
note: Jeremiah applies the fulfilment test (35:9): a prophet of peace is known as truly sent when his word comes; cf. Deut 18:21–22.

title: Jeremiah is told to answer Shemaiah and rebuke the priest Zephaniah
speaker: the Lord
note: Greek-order text: 'I did not send you' to Shemaiah; Zephaniah reminded of his appointment as overseer to confine raving prophets (36:26).

title: Restored Israel is told to plant vineyards in Samaria and praise
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
note: Imperatives in the restoration oracle ('plant and praise'), like the recorded calls at 38:7 and 38:21.

title: The Rechabites recount Jonadab’s rule on houses, crops and tents
speaker: the Rechabites
note: 42:11 completes their account: the resolve 'Come in, let us enter Jerusalem' explains why they now live in the city.

title: God sends Jeremiah to ask why Judah refuses instruction
speaker: the Lord
note: 42:14 is the message’s content: the Rechabites kept Jonadab’s command, Judah did not listen. 42:15 already has its own record.

title: The officials summon Baruch to read the scroll to them
speaker: the officials (rulers) of Judah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 'Take… the roll… and come'; 'Read it again to us' (43:15, context); then 'Let us certainly report all these words to the king.'

title: Zedekiah sends envoys asking Jeremiah to pray for them
speaker: King Zedekiah, through Jehucal and Zephaniah
note: A separate occasion from 21:2 (ot-jeremiah-v21-2): different envoys and a request for intercession.

title: Jeremiah begs Zedekiah not to send him back to Jonathan’s house
speaker: Jeremiah

title: Zedekiah orders Jeremiah held in the prison court with daily bread
speaker: King Zedekiah
note: Reported royal order in a context verse (not a listed candidate); no record covers 44:21.

title: The officials demand Jeremiah’s death, and Zedekiah yields him to them
speaker: the officials of Judah
note: 'Let that man be killed!'; the king answers 'He is in your hands' (45:5). Recording the demand does not approve it.

title: Zedekiah orders Ebed-melech to take thirty men and rescue Jeremiah
speaker: King Zedekiah
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours

title: Ebed-melech tells Jeremiah to put the rags beneath the ropes
speaker: Ebed-melech
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Uncovered directive two verses after the candidate (not listed): 'Put these beneath the ropes. Jeremiah did so.'

title: The survivors ask Jeremiah to seek the Lord’s direction
speaker: Johanan, the commanders and the survivors
note: The request begins in 49:2: 'Pray to the Lord your God for these survivors.'

title: God sends Ezekiel to the rebellious house of Israel
speaker: the Lord
note: Ezekiel’s call proper ('stand on your feet… I am sending you… you will say to them'); only 2:6 and 2:8 are recorded.

title: God tells Ezekiel to listen and eat what he is given
speaker: the Lord
note: 3:1–3 completes the same directive: 'eat this scroll, then go and speak to the sons of Israel.'

title: Ezekiel is sent to speak the Lord’s words to the exiles
speaker: the Lord
note: Repeated commission ('go, enter the house of Israel, and speak My words'), with the warning they will not listen (3:7, P02206).

title: Ezekiel is sent to speak the Lord’s words to the exiles
speaker: the Lord
note: 3:10–11 is one charge: 'take into your heart all the words… and go, enter the captivity.'

title: Ezekiel is told to depict Jerusalem under siege
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 4:1 begins the same sign: take a brick and draw the city Jerusalem on it.

title: Ezekiel is told to lie on his side as a sign of Israel’s guilt
speaker: the Lord
note: 4:6 completes the sign: lie on the right side forty days for Judah, a day for a year.

title: Ezekiel is told to announce that the end has come on Israel
speaker: the Lord
note: Order to proclaim ('say, Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel'); such orders are Commission records at 6:3 and 11:4.

title: The land is told to sound the trumpet as judgment comes
speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Greek-text imperative ('Sound the trumpet and judge everything') inside the judgment oracle; compare recorded alarm calls Jeremiah 4:5 and 6:1.

title: Ezekiel covers his face and goes out as a sign
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 12:3–5 hold the rest of the exile sign (ready baggage by day, dig through the wall); 12:7 reports his compliance.

title: Ezekiel is told to eat and drink in anguish as a sign
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Sign-act; its meaning (12:19) has a Study Context record, the command itself has none.

title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Israel’s false prophets
speaker: the Lord
note: Commission with the opening woe on those who prophesy from their own heart; 13:8 and 13:11 are Study Context only.

title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the women who prophesy falsely
speaker: the Lord
note: 'Set your face firmly against the daughters of your people'; the 13:18 woe is Study Context only.

summary: 45 findings (29 new, 14 extend, 2 parallel), mostly unrecorded prophetic commissions, sign-acts and narrative requests or royal orders in Jeremiah 36–49 and Ezekiel 2–13; judgment and promise oracles need nothing.
